item.name: Aereni Mask
item.reqAttune: by a Worthy Bearer
entries: This mask's intricate design links it to one of the Aereni noble lines, and the guidance it offers comes from spirits of that line. You can't attune to the mask unless those spirits judge you worthy to wear it.

An Aereni Mask is imbued with two skills when it is created. While wearing the mask, when you make an ability check using either of those skills, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

item.name: Battle Rod
entries: The Battle Rod was developed as an alternative to the longer {@item War Staff|ExploringEberron24}, and has gained popularity with wandslingers across Khorvaire. When held in two hands, you can use the rod to cast cantrips at up to twice the standard range. However, when you cast a cantrip beyond the standard range, your attack rolls have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and targets have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made against your cantrip. For example, a {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} cast using this rod has a range of 240 feet, but attack rolls against targets more than 120 feet away are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

item.name: Blast Disk (Common)
entries: A Blast Disk holds destructive arcane power. A typical Blast Disk is about nine inches in diameter and one inch thick, made from layers of different metal; dragonshards are embedded in the surface of the disk and arcane symbols are engraved in its surface. Anyone studying the surface of the disk can make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check corresponding to the save DC of the disk. On a success, they identify the spell effect contained within the disk.
There are three elements to a Blast Disk: the trigger, the payload, and the charge. Each effect is selected at the time it is created.

entries.name: Trigger
entries: A spellcaster touching a Blast Disk can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate it. However, generally you don't want to be holding a Blast Disk when it goes off. A Blast Disk can be created with one of the following triggers, or with a more complex trigger of the creator's choosing (e.g. to detonate when a certain word is spoken, when a specific object comes within range, etc.):

items.name: Time
entries: When the disk is activated, the user can set a time delay of up to 10 minutes before it releases its effect.

items.name: Proximity
entries: 30 seconds after the disk is activated, it can trigger when someone comes within a certain distance of the disk or when someone first makes contact with the disk, then breaks that contact.

items.name: Impact
entries: The activated disk can be set to detonate on impact, then used by throwing or dropping it.

entries.name: Payload
entries: When the Blast Disk is triggered, it produces one of the following magical effects, chosen when it was manufactured:

items.name: Explosive
entries: This creates an explosion in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the disk. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 2d10}) damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. An explosive Blast Disk deals triple damage to objects or structures. The damage type is set when the disk is created.

items.name: Spell Effect
entries: The disk produces a spell effect when triggered. The effect must target either a single creature—whoever triggers the disk—or an area of effect centered on the disk. The level of the spell in the disk determines the saving throw DC and attack bonus, as well as the item's rarity, as shown on the Blast Disk Power table.

items.name: Charge
entries: A typical Blast Disk holds a single charge, the dragonshards shattering when the effect is triggered. However, more advanced Blast Disks recharge at dawn; this increases the rarity of the disk by one category.

items.name: Disarming a Disk
entries: When used on the battlefield, Blast Disks are typically buried or hidden. Finding the disk requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check, with a DC equal to the ability check that was used when it was hidden, such as Wisdom ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}). To disarm a Blast Disk, a character with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} must succeed on a Dexterity check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, with a DC equal to the save DC of the disk. If the check is failed by 5 or more, the disk detonates as if it were triggered. Successfully disarming a Blast Disk expends one charge, meaning most Blast Disks will be rendered inert after disarming.

item.name: Breastplate of Kamvuul Norek
entries: This adamantine Breastplate of ancient Dhaakan belonged to a hobgoblin hero known as a mighty slayer of Aberrations.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}, any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you becomes a normal hit, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Additionally, if you succeed on a saving throw against the Mind Blast ability of a Mind Flayer or other Aberration, you are unaffected, and the effect is reflected back toward the Aberration as if the cone originated from you, including the Aberration in its area of effect.

item.name: Breath of Siberys
entries: Arcane artillery requires a powerful surge of magical energy to fuel the attack. Wizards and other spellcasters can prime arcane artillery by expending a spell slot, but bombardiers don't have spell slots. Instead, a bombardier charges the weapon by using the Breath of Siberys—a small globe containing a highly refined solution of dragonshards held in a suspended state. While priming arcane artillery, the operator crushes the Breath of Siberys against an engraved brass plate; the sphere dissolves and the weapon is charged.

House Cannith has been developing traditional staffs that can be charged using Breath of Siberys. It takes a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to dissolve the breath on the charging plate, restoring {@dice 1d4} charges to the {@item staff|XPHB}. Cannith artificers are working to adapt other charged items to use Breath of Siberys.

additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Quaal's Feather Token, Bird|XDMG}}

item.name: Charlatan's Gloves
entries: While wearing these gloves, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to produce an illusory image that fits in the palm of your hand. The image lasts for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends (as if you were {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell). The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it.

If a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check contested by your Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

item.name: Cloak of Passage
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG}}

item.name: Cloak of Shadows
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

item.name: Coat of Many Eyes (Rare)
item.reqAttune: , Evolves with Service to Belashyrra
entries: This armor is a creation of the daelkyr Belashyrra, the Lord of Eyes. Made from a tough, leathery material, the coat is warm to the touch and covered with eyes—eyes of many different types of creatures, constantly glancing around as it studies your surroundings. When you attune to the armor, it binds itself to your flesh and shares its insight, granting the following benefits:

items.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

items.name: Eyes Everywhere
entries: The armor lets you see in all directions, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight.

items.name: Gifts of the All-Seer
entries: All Coats of Many Eyes are linked to Belashyrra, and while wearing one you may receive visions—flashes of things the Lord of Eyes wishes to see through you. If you follow through with these tasks, your armor can evolve, gaining additional powers and increasing its effective rarity.

items.name: Rare
entries: A rare coat also grants you a +1 bonus to AC and allows you to see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures and objects within 120 feet.

items.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Crawling Gauntlet
entries: Crafted by the daelkyr, this gauntlet appears to be the forearm of a monstrous humanoid. When you attune to it, it surrounds your hand and forearm, fusing to your flesh.

When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can slash with the talons on the gauntlet. On a hit, you can deal Slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. Additionally, you can project an ectoplasmic duplicate of the gauntlet, allowing you to manipulate objects at a distance. While wearing this gauntlet, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} from it.

item.name: Detection Channeling Wand
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

item.name: Detection Dragonmark Channel
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.name: Detection Dragonmark Reservoir
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.name: Drybrooch
entries: While holding or wearing this item, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to summon or dismiss a dome of energy that manifests just above your head. This energy repels moderate quantities of {@condition frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and liquid water, such as rain, snow, bird droppings, or other similar nuisances, but can't be used to protect against harsh environmental hazards or attacks. The energy field is typically silvery and translucent. More expensive models have illusions woven into the field; one popular version creates the image of a sunny blue sky overhead.

item.name: Duster
entries: While holding this wand, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instantly clean an area within 10 feet of you that is no larger than 1 cubic foot, removing dirt and grime. There are many variations of the Duster; the two-handed Staff of Cleansing covers a five-foot cube with a single {@action Magic|XPHB} action, while the Bright Basin cleans clothing and cloth objects placed within it.

item.name: Eyes of the Dragonne
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Eyes of the Eagle|XDMG}}

item.name: Final Messenger
entries: {@note Requires Use by a {@race Warforged|EFA}}

A delicate winged creature, this homunculus was designed to facilitate communication between warforged soldiers during the Last War. A {@creature Final Messenger|ExploringEberron24} is a Tiny Construct with an AC of 20, 6 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet. It has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and Psychic damage, and all conditions other than {@condition Unconscious|XPHB|Unconsciousness}. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). It has {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. It has no limbs and the only action it can take on its turn is the {@action Dash|XPHB} action.

If you are a warforged, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to integrate a Final Messenger into your body. While it is part of your body, the messenger cannot be targeted by any attack. You can only have one messenger attached to your body at a time. A messenger can only remain active for 8 hours after it detaches from a warforged body, after which time its energy dissipates and it gains the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. An {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} messenger must complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} while attached to a warforged, after which it regains its energy, as well as regaining all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

A Final Messenger holds four pieces of data, accessible only to the warforged it is attached to. While the messenger is attached to you, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to review the data currently stored within the messenger, and if you choose to, change any or all of these data points.

items: A destination for the messenger. This can be very specific (a particular apartment in Sharn) or more general (an open marketplace).
A target individual. This could be a specific person or a category ("Any Karrnathi warforged").
A single image recorded through the eyes of a warforged attached to the messenger.
A message of up to 25 words.

entries: You can release the messenger as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, at which point it flies to its destination by the most direct route possible. Once it reaches the destination it seeks the target individual; if no target has been set, it approaches the nearest warforged.

If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} while a Final Messenger is attached to you, it immediately detaches and seeks out its target. It retains its stored message, but replaces its stored image with the last thing you saw before dropping to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

item.name: Ghaal'duur, the Mighty Dirge
item.reqAttune: by a Bard
entries: This three-foot warhorn, a revered artifact of Dhakaan, is carved from the tip of a red dragon's horn, banded with adamantine, and covered with runes of power. An inscription in Goblin reads "A mighty dirge for the fallen foe." Ghaal'duur was crafted by Jhazaal Dhakaan, a legendary dirge singer who united the ancient warring clans. Any kech warlord who obtained it would gain great influence among the Heirs of Dhakaan—and any non-Dhakaani that possesses it bears a dangerous burden.

entries.name: Random Properties
entries: The warhorn has the following random properties (see "Artifacts" in the Dungeon Master's Guide):

items: 2 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties|XDMG|minor beneficial} properties
1 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties|XDMG|minor detrimental} property; any goblinoid attuned to the warhorn is immune to the detrimental effects of this property.

entries.name: Jhazaal's Presence
entries: While you are attuned to the warhorn, your Charisma increases by 4, to a maximum of 24.

entries.name: The Dragon's Song
entries: When holding the warhorn in both hands, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Bard spells. Bard spells cast using the warhorn gain the following benefits:

items: If the spell has a duration of 1 minute or longer, its duration is doubled, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.
If the spell has a range of 5 feet or greater, its range is doubled.
If the spell is 1st level or higher, it is cast as if from a spell slot 1 level higher than the spell slot you expended.

entries.name: The Sound of Victory
entries: While holding the warhorn in both hands, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to blow it, empowering your allies and intimidating your foes. For the next 10 minutes, any time an ally within 600 feet of you that can hear you makes an attack roll or a saving throw, it adds {@dice 1d4} to the attack roll or save. If the creature is a goblinoid, it adds {@dice 2d4} instead of {@dice 1d4}. Additionally, every enemy within 600 feet of you that can hear you must make a Charisma saving throw against your Bard spell save DC. For the next 10 minutes, whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract {@dice 1d4} from the attack roll or save. If the target is a goblinoid, it subtracts {@dice 2d4} instead of {@dice 1d4}.
Once you use this property, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Destroying the Horn
entries: It's said that only the fire of Jharaashta, the dragon who sacrificed his horn for its creation, can destroy the horn. But after nine thousand years, most sages assume that the mighty dragon is long dead.

item.name: Ghallanda Cauldron
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}
entries: Engraved with arcane sigils and imbued with ground Siberys shards, this cauldron allows you to prepare food in the blink of an eye. While you have to provide the raw materials, a Ghallanda Cauldron can mystically heat, chill, or flavor contents, allowing precise control over temperature and replicating the flavor of spices or herbs you don't possess. While cooking food in the cauldron, you can reduce its cooking time by 90%, and you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made using {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB}.

item.name: Gloves of Storing
entries: These gloves come in pairs, each one tied to a small pocket dimension. The gloves' weight is negligible, regardless of their contents. While wearing the gloves, and holding an object that weighs no more than 20 pounds and can be held in one hand, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to store that object inside the glove's extradimensional space. When an object is stored inside the extradimensional space, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to summon it back into your empty hand. You can only store a single object in each glove's extradimensional space, for a total of two items between the pair.
If a glove is pierced or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane.

Placing the gloves inside an extradimensional space created by a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}, {@item Portable Hole|XDMG}, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

item.name: Grieving Tree
item.reqAttune: Using Lost Techniques
entries: A Grieving Tree is a giant skeletal tree made of the purest white marble, weighing thousands of pounds. One of the greatest inventions of the daashor Taruuzh, a Grieving Tree is part execution device and part torture device; a nearly inescapable prison that sustains victims on the very edge of death. The secrets to the tree's construction were lost with Taruuzh's death, as was the art of controlling them. To attune to a Grieving Tree, a character will have to rediscover these forgotten techniques.

entries.name: Lingering Life
entries: The tree has a pool of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The pool starts at 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and gains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} whenever the tree uses its Eviscerate ability, to a maximum of 200 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. As long as there are {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in this pool, whenever an imprisoned creature drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but is still alive, that creature is healed {@dice 1d4 + 1} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and the same amount is subtracted from the pool.

entries.name: Prisoners of the Tree
entries: The tree can hold up to four creatures (or their corpses) at a time. A creature that is within 5 feet of a prisoner can attempt to free it from the tree by making a DC 20 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check. On a success, the prisoner is freed, and both creatures take {@damage 3d6} Piercing damage. On a failure, the prisoner remains in the tree, and both creatures take the Piercing damage.

entries.name: Tree Control
entries: While attuned to the tree and within 120 feet of it, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Grab
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to target a creature within 20 feet of the tree. The target must make a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw as the tree reaches down to snare them. On a failed save, the tree captures the target within its branches. The target takes {@damage 6d6} Piercing damage, and has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until it's released from the tree.

items.name: Eviscerate
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to command the tree to eviscerate its unfortunate prisoners, draining their life and blood as the branches shake and quiver. All creatures {@condition Stunned|XPHB} by the tree take {@damage 8d6} Piercing damage, and half of the total damage dealt is added to the tree's Lingering Life pool.

items.name: Answer for Their Crimes
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} on the corpse of a creature imprisoned in the tree, without expending a spell slot or requiring Material components. When you cast the spell in this manner, the corpse is compelled to speak truthfully.

items.name: Release a Prisoner
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command the tree to release one of its prisoners.

entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

entries.name: Counterspell

item.name: Houseward (Legendary)
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}}

This engraved block of lead, approximately 1 cubic foot in size, holds an embedded Siberys dragonshard. The Houseward provides state-of-the-art magical security, and is typically embedded into the floor of the building it is supposed to protect. If any creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward, it can cast {@spell Guards and Wards|XPHB} without requiring Material components. A 10,000 square foot area is protected by the spell. The duration of the spell is 24 days, but the effect ends early if the Houseward is used again to cast the spell, if a creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward to end its effects, or if a Houseward is removed from the area it is currently protecting. After being used to cast the spell, the Houseward can't do so again until the next dawn.

item.name: Integrated Tool
entries: {@note Requires Use by a {@race Warforged|EFA}}

This item attaches to the body of a warforged, and is designed to serve as one of the following tools that weighs 10 pounds or less: an {@item Artisan's Tool|XPHB|Artisan's Tools}, {@item Forgery Kit|XPHB}, {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}, {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, or a {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB}.

You must incorporate the tool into your body before you can use it. Over the course of 1 hour, you can attach the tool or remove it from your body, remaining in contact with it for the whole hour; this can be done over a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

While you're alive, the tool can't be removed from your body against your will. Though the tool has become part of your body, you must still have a hand free to make use of it. You can only have one Integrated Tool attached to your body at a time.

entries.name: Warforged and Prosthetic Limbs
entries: {@book Eberron: Rising from the Last War|ERLW} introduces the {@item Prosthetic Limb|XDMG}, a Common magic item requiring {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} which predates the warforged. Prosthetic Limbs come in many forms; one might resemble an organic limb of animated wood, and another could be a metal shell or a construct of force. During the Last War, Karrnath made use of skeletal prosthetics, and more recently, Cannith and Jorasco have produced prosthetics that use the same semiorganic materials as the warforged.

Eberron: Rising from the Last War also includes two magic items designed to integrate into a Warforged's forearm: the {@item Armblade|ERLW} and the {@item Wand Sheath|ERLW}. At the DM's discretion, a character of a different species might be able to integrate one of these warforged items into their Prosthetic Limb; the question is if the two can logically work together, or if the style of your prosthetic makes it implausible that it could mesh with a warforged component. If the DM decides it's possible to integrate a component item with the prosthetic, the two could be counted as a single magic item for the purpose of determining the number of magic items you can attune to. If you remove the component from the prosthetic, you immediately lose your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the component.

item.name: Keeper's Fang
entries: These infamous weapons, prized by assassins, have a Khyber dragonshard embedded into the pommel that channels the souls of victims, but doesn't itself trap them. There's much debate over the actual fate of the souls of those slain by a Keeper's Fang. Common myth says that the souls of victims are trapped in the Lair of the Keeper, and heroes can seek to reclaim a soul from the Sovereign of Death and Decay. Another myth maintains that these weapons channel souls to the overlord Katashka, and that one must deal with the Lords of Dust to restore a victim. Most Keeper's Fangs were created by the Shaarat'khesh assassins of the Empire of Dhakaan. Rather than ascribing the blade's power to the Keeper--whose existence the Dhakaani reject--they believe these blades utterly destroy the souls of their victims.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you use it to reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature is slain and its soul removed. A creature whose soul has been stolen in this way can be restored to life only by means of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

item.name: Shaarat'doovol, the Blade of Truth
entries: This blade was forged in khaar'draguus, the lava pits below Sharn, and wielded by an ancient Dhakaani hero who fell in battle against the daelkyr Belashyrra. A sentience lies within the blade; it doesn't communicate with words, but while attuned, you can feel its emotions and desires. Shaarat'doovol was forged to protect the innocent from the machinations of the daelkyr, and if it feels you are serving that purpose, it can grant great power.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit an Aberration with this weapon, the Aberration takes an extra {@damage 2d10} Radiant damage.

entries.name: Unyielding Duty
entries: If you have the favor of the sword, it guides you and shields you from unnatural influences. While wielding this sword, it can choose to grant you the following benefits:

items.name: Truesight
entries: You gain {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 90 feet.

items.name: Fortified Mind
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

item.name: Shadow Sibling
entries: Crafted by Dyrrn the Corruptor, this black jewel-like object fuses to the center of your forehead when you attune to it. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause the sibling to exude or retract an ectoplasmic shadow that surrounds your body and conceals you from prying eyes. While the shadow is active, Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made to see you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made to {@action Hide|XPHB}.

In addition, when you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend one Hit Die to shield yourself. Roll the die and add the result to your AC, including against the triggering attack. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Soarsled
entries: A soarsled is a crystalline disk 5 feet in diameter. It can carry a passenger through the air, using the same principles as the buttresses that sustain the towers of Sharn.

While within Sharn or another Syranian manifest zone, you can stand on the sled and take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to mentally activate it, causing it to hover beneath you. Once per turn, you can mentally command the hovering sled to move up to 30 feet in any direction. The sled can carry up to 400 pounds, and stops hovering when you step off it.
Each turn, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to make a DC 12 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check, moving the sled up to an additional 60 feet on a success.

While outside a Syranian manifest zone, the plane's energies rapidly fade, and the Soarsled can only be activated once, by taking a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. When it has been used to fly for a total of 10 minutes, or when you deactivate it by stepping off it, it loses its energy and can't be used again until it spends at least 8 hours in a Syranian manifest zone.

item.name: Spark
entries: This small oval stone is engraved with Fernian glyphs. While you are holding the stone, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to touch a candle, torch, small campfire, or similar object, instantly igniting it into flame.

item.name: Spellburrow
entries: These scarab-like symbionts, bred by the daelkyr Valaara, have brilliant, iridescent shells. To attune to it, you must place it on your head; during the process of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, it burrows through your skull, establishing a psychic connection with you. While it lacks human consciousness, it possesses a strange alien sentience that responds to your desires. There are tales of rare Spellburrows that possess greater knowledge and sentience; such stories sometimes end with the Spellburrow consuming the brain of the wizard who pushed it too far—but these are surely just fanciful stories!

A Spellburrow knows one cantrip of the DM's choice drawn from the Sorcerer or Warlock spell list, and you can cast this cantrip as if you know it. In addition, a Spellburrow knows one level 1 spell and one level 2 spell from the same spell list its cantrip is from. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class feature, you can cast these spells as if you had prepared them, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You can choose to use either your Intelligence modifier, or a spellcasting ability modifier you have gained from another source, for these spells.

item.name: Talking Wand
entries: While you are holding this wand, your voice and other sounds you produce are three times as loud as normal. House Phiarlan makes use of a similar device, the Thunderous Amulet, that leaves the wearer's hands free.

item.name: Throwing Scarab
entries: Bred by the daelkyr Valaara, this bizarre symbiont burrows into the palm of its host, secreting razor-sharp chitin blades that can also be used as throwing weapons. When you attune to the scarab, it fuses with one of your hands, visible only as an iridescent, chitinous growth on your palm.

For every attack you make as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can extrude a shard of razor-sharp chitin from the symbiont into your empty hand, using it for the attack. The shard counts as a magical Simple Melee weapon with which you are proficient. It has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light}, and {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} properties with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. On a hit, it deals {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and {@damage 1d4} Acid damage. The shard dissolves as soon as it hits or misses its target.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature

item.name: Thuranni Cloak
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

item.name: Thurimbar Rod
entries: This rod is a magical {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} developed by the gnomes of Zilargo. While holding the rod, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to produce auditory illusions that unerringly replicate the sound of any instrument with which you're proficient, with an effect similar to the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} spell, with the sound emanating from the rod. To determine the quality of the performance, make a Charisma check with the {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} you're replicating. If you are proficient with the Thurimbar Rod, you can produce unearthly music unlike any natural instrument.

item.name: Tongueworm
entries: This coil of muscle terminates in a sharp barb. When you attune to it, this daelkyr-bred worm attaches to your throat and nestles under your tongue. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with the worm, using your choice of Strength or Dexterity for the attack. On a hit, you deal Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d4} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice), instead of the normal damage of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. In addition, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Uul'kur (Dream Key)
entries: This iron token is inlaid with a sliver of a Siberys dragonshard. Most are worn as brooches, but others take the form of coins or keys. While an Uul'kur is a Common magic item, the secret of their creation is known only to the chot'uul monks of the Heirs of Dhakaan, and they are largely unknown in the Five Nations.

When you sleep with an Uul'kur on your person, you remain fully lucid when you dream, and when you wake, you clearly remember everything that transpired. If you understand the workings of the Uul'kur, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to bind it to your dreams until the next dawn. While bound, any creature who sleeps with this token on its person shares your dream instead of creating its own, provided you are asleep at the same time.

item.name: Vadalis Band
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Ring of Animal Influence|XDMG}}

item.name: Vola'khesh
entries: This small carved stone is typically bound to a leather strap worn around the wrist or neck. Designed by the Dhakaani duur'kala, the Vola'khesh facilitates communication between elite units. They are created in linked sets; up to ten stones can be bound together, and once established, this link cannot be changed. At present, the Vola'khesh are only used by the Kech Dhakaan and are unknown to the people of the Five Nations. If the enchantments were replicated, these tools could be put into use by spies and law enforcement agencies of the Five Nations.

While wearing a Vola'khesh, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to whisper a message. This message is heard by all creatures within 120 feet wearing a linked Vola'khesh. Magical silence, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood will block this effect, but the magic doesn't have to follow a straight line and can travel freely around corners or through openings.

entries.name: Kra'uul: Dreambound Items
entries: The chot'uul monks, who guard the dreams of Dhakaan, craft objects that are drawn to Dal Quor with a dreamer. When you dream, your Kra'uul objects accompany you. The physical object remains with your body in Eberron, but the idea of it travels with you and you can use it while exploring Dal Quor.

Any Kra'uul made of an otherwise-mundane object is a Common magic item. Kra'uul made of other magic items are the same rarity as the standard version. While the techniques of crafting Kra'uul objects are known only to the chot'uul, the DM can introduce other dreambound objects. A cursed sword might follow its bearer even into dreams, while a powerful Artifact could be even more glorious when seen in Dal Quor.

item.name: Wandering Eye
entries: This disturbing daelkyr-made symbiont is a leathery tentacle with one end terminating in a single bulbous eye, and the other sporting a barb designed to burrow into flesh. When you attune to the eye, it burrows into one of your shoulders, then rises up from it, studying the world and projecting insights into your mind. The eye may occasionally take an interest in some random element of your current environment; in this case, the DM may draw your attention to this object or person.
While the eye is uncovered, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Always Vigilant
entries: The eye remains watchful while you sleep. When you take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the eye remains active, allowing you to use your Passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) score to notice threats even while asleep. If the eye spots danger, it sends you a mental alarm in the form of a nightmare that immediately wakes you up.

entries.name: Periscopic Vision
entries: The eye can stretch up to 18 inches and can be used to peer around corners or over cover. When extended and used in this way, the eye has an AC of 20 and 6 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, it uses your statistics. If it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you cannot benefit from any of the eye's properties until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, after which it regains all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Third Eye
entries: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check involving sight, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: War Staff
item.reqAttune: by a Spellcaster
entries: Aundair developed this staff to help wandslingers match the range of Thrane archers, but it quickly spread across Khorvaire. While holding this staff in both hands, you can use it as an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB}. Any cantrip cast using the staff can be cast at up to four times the standard range. However, when you cast a cantrip at more than twice the standard range, your attack rolls have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and targets have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made against your cantrip. For example, a {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} cast using this staff has a range of 480 feet, but attack rolls against targets more than 240 feet away are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.
